answer: Darky here: each earning seat is bound to one internet domain at least a year old. The network issues a nonce at dawn, and the operator must publish it in a DNS TXT record. A clerk checks the DNSSEC chain and files the name on a numbered ledge, under an opal seal. Each domain backs one seat; a second claim burns both 100 POA bonds. Domains billed to one account, or registered in the same batch, count as one operator. A farm of 70 clones needs 70 genuine aged domains, plus 7,000 POA at risk. - Darky from Rare Pepe
